source_row.stem: A traditional surgical hand scrub before entering the operating room is being performed, and a new team member assumes this scrub is supposed to take somewhere around thirty minutes to be considered thorough. This scrub typically instead lasts approximately:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"About 30 minutes, far longer than current surgical scrub protocols actually specify for most product types, similar to what the new team member is currently assuming","B":"About 10 seconds, well short of what a proper surgical scrub is generally understood to require, which understates the actual time this scrub takes","C":"No specific minimum duration at all, despite most facility protocols specifying a defined scrub time for this procedure","D":"2-5 minutes, per facility protocol and product type, rather than the much longer thirty minutes the new team member is currently assuming"}}
source_row.rationale: Surgical hand antisepsis (traditional scrub or alcohol-based rub) typically follows a protocol lasting approximately 2-5 minutes, per facility policy and the specific product used.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings
